newsitem.title: UK: NWE gas oil surges higher on tight supply.
newsitem.headline: NWE gas oil surges higher on tight supply.

text.p: NWE gas oil surged on Friday as benchmark IPE futures soared on concerns over a shortage of prompt supply in northwest Europe ahead of the September contract's expiry next week.
The September IPE contract ended $7.0 higher at $220.00 a tonne.
Prompt heating oil barges traded at Sept IPE +$5. Premiums were put at Sept IPE +$5/+$6.
Traders said planned refinery maintenance, low water levels on Rhine and increased demand from German end-users had all conspired to tighten supply and raise prices.
"Only those who really need product are coming in. A lot of German heating oil dealers who were waiting for prices to dip appear to have been caught out," one trader said.
Second half September premiums were put at Sept IPE +$1/+$2. One second half barge was done at Sept IPE +$1.25.
DIN cargo premiums were also firm on the tightness. Traders said put them at roughly Oct IPE +$4.50/+$5.0 a tonne.
Traders said a brisk trade in Russian cargoes had been done on Thursday in an attempt to cover 0.2 percent shorts. Premiums were put at about Sept IPE +$1.0 cif ARA.
